entries.title: Jeremiah 15:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Cast them out - I am not able to abide the sight of them, therefore let them go forth.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Manasseh - Manasseh is here named as the son of Hezekiah for his shame, because of his degeneracy from so good a parent; it is expressly said, 2Kings 23:26, that not withstanding Josiah's reformation, yet the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his wrath, kindled against Judah, for the provocations of Manasseh.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I am weary - I am resolved to bear no longer.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A fan - Not a purging fan by affliction, to separate their chaff and dross from them, but a scattering fan. In the gates - This is added in pursuit of the metaphor of fanning, men usually chusing barn - doors to fan at, that they may have the advantage of the wind.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Their widows - The prophet still speaks of things to come as if present. In Jehoiakim's time we read of no such plenty of widows; they were multiplied when the city was besieged and taken in Zedekiah's time, to a great number, hyperbolically compared to the sands of the sea. The mother - Jerusalem was the mother of the Jewish people, against whom, Nebuchadnezzar the spoiler, at noon - day, was sent.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Seven - Seven signifies many: the prophet complains, that the country of Judah, that had been very numerous in people, now grew feeble. While - In the midst of her prosperity. Confounded - A part of them were confounded by the judgments of God which came upon them before their captivity.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I have not - I have done them no wrong, yet they speak of me all manner of evil.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy remnant - The latter words of the verse expound the former; for by remnant is meant the remnant of days that Jeremiah had to live.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The northern iron - As the northern iron and steel is the hardest, and no iron could break that, so God having edged and hardened their enemies, the Chaldeans, all opposition to them would signify nothing.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The substance - All thy precious things shall be spoiled, there shall be no price taken for the redemption of them.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thou knowest - My sincerity, or my sufferings. Visit me - With thy love.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy words - The words which from time to time thou didst reveal to me, were by me greedily digested. I am called - I became a prophet by thy authority, therefore, do thou own and defend me.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I sat not - God had all along filled his mouth with such dreadful messages, that his whole prophetical life had been to him a time of mourning and solitude, a time when he sat alone, mourning and weeping in secret for the wrath of God revealed to him against his people.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Why - Jeremiah, though a great prophet, was (as Elijah) a man subject to like passions with other men.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: If thou - These are God's words to the prophet, rebuking his distrust in God, and promising him, that if he did return from his distrust in God's providence, he would restore him to the former favour he had with him, and he should be his prophet to reveal his mind to the people; and that if he would separate the precious truths of God from the vile conceits of men, then God would continue him as his prophet, to speak in his name to the people. But - He charges the prophet to keep his ground, and not to go over to wicked men.

entries.title: Jeremiah 15:21–16:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The wicked - The wicked Jews. The terrible - And the power of the terrible Chaldeans.
